STAGED_SERIES_PROMPT:
Staged review of this epoch. An epoch is one frozen run of this review: its evidence, its claims and its tasks. The role text above defines the scientific criteria, the evidence rules and the schema of the completed review, and it describes the whole review. This call carries one task of a series that performs the review in stages, because its evidence, its required output or its running time does not fit one call of this route. For this call, the task text below and the staged rules replace the response shape and the request-turn rules of the role text; its scientific criteria and its evidence rules still apply. This call is a fresh input: no earlier turn is replayed, and nothing reached you before this packet. The work of earlier tasks reaches you only as the records in this packet, which the harness built from verified outputs of earlier tasks. Verified means that a record passed the harness's checks of shape, identity, delivery and quotation; it does not mean that its scientific content is right.

staged_review describes this task. task holds the frozen task envelope: id, type (frame, read, combine, original_check, integrate, answer or final), scope, claim_ids, occurrence_ids, card_ids, group_ids, segment_task_ids, obligation_ids, child_ids and context_roots. claims lists the claims assigned to this task: a claim is one statement taken verbatim from the frame, with an id, its kind (claim, condition or definition), the conditions and definitions it needs, the claims it depends on, its context_root and the decisions it bears on. decisions lists the decisions of this role, each with the claims it requires and the values the record permits. units lists the delivered evidence units: a unit is one item of the evidence lists with the artifact bodies it owns, identified by occurrence_id, key and index; each of its texts is a source with a source_id and a span object. index lists the units this task may name beyond its own input, and index_root names the complete paged index. output_characters is the number of characters your response may use. The frame is the problem record the role text names: statement, resolution criteria, definitions, value paragraphs, self-assessment, openness finding, attempt, results, citations and material objections.

Your response is one JSON object whose keys are the record lists the task text names. Every record has an id. A new id is unique in this epoch and begins with the task id; a reference names an id that this packet delivers or that this response defines. The harness checks every record by its shape, its identities, what this packet delivered and its quotations. A record that fails a check receives no credit; the other records of the response stand on their own. Complete the assigned entries in the order the packet lists them. An entry you do not reach stays pending and goes to a further task; a partial record for it earns nothing. Keep within output_characters.

Read every delivered original completely before you write its records. Keep every condition under which a source establishes something. Judge the original in front of you, not what you expect it to say. Do not assess the problem in this task unless the task text asks for a decision.
STAGED_SHARED_RECORDS_PROMPT:
Shared records of this series.

A quotation is {source_id, text}: source_id copied from the delivered source, text copied character for character from that source. The harness finds the text in the source after it changes each character to its NFKC form and each run of white space to one space, binds the exact span and keeps the source characters. A quotation the harness does not find invalidates the record that carries it. A whole short source is a valid quotation.

A ground is a quotation, or the id of a record that this packet delivers as resolved: a cell, an original check, a retrieval or a conclusion. The task text says which grounds a record accepts.

A card records what one unit establishes and its bearing on the assigned claims: {id, occurrence_id, kind, establishes, evidence_type, conclusions, conditions, judgments, critical_spans, findings, unresolved, dependencies, fragment_ids}, with the optional fields premises, reasoning, negative_observation, examined_scope, no_statement_reason and reconciliation_id. occurrence_id is copied from the unit. kind is full for a card that covers the whole unit and every claim of the epoch, and fragment otherwise. establishes states in your words what the source establishes. evidence_type is established_result, conjecture, computation, assertion, reviewer_deduction or reviewer_observation, the kind of the main content. A reviewer_deduction carries premises (grounds) and reasoning (text). A card whose main content is an absence (the source does not state, prove or cite something) has evidence_type reviewer_observation, negative_observation true and examined_scope naming what you examined; an absence is your observation, never a quotation. conclusions and conditions are lists of {id, text, grounds}: a conclusion is one thing the source establishes, a condition is one hypothesis, parameter range, stated input or version under which it holds. critical_spans lists the quotations that decide the assigned claims; when none exists, no_statement_reason explains why no statement of this source decides any assigned claim. judgments lists one cell per assigned claim. findings lists the ids of the findings you return in the findings list. unresolved lists {text, claim_ids, needs}, the questions the source raises and does not settle, where needs names a unit of index, another segment, or the evidence the epoch lacks. dependencies lists the ids of retrievals or original checks the card's conclusions wait for, or is empty. fragment_ids is empty for a fragment card and lists the fragment cards of the unit for a full card.

A cell records the judgment of one claim against one unit: {id, occurrence_id, claim_id, status, reason, grounds, scope, context_root}, with the optional fields source_subject, segment_ids, reconciliation_id and dependencies. context_root is copied from the claim. status is supported, contradicted, no_bearing or unresolved. reason explains the judgment from the grounds; a condition that restricts the claim appears in the reason and in the card's conditions. no_bearing means the examined source has no bearing on the claim: source_subject names the subject and the scope of the source, and reason states its relation to the claim. unresolved means relevant material cannot settle the judgment within the delivered scope; reason names the missing scope or the open dependency. grounds are quotations; a supported, contradicted or no_bearing cell has at least one, and for no_bearing it shows the subject of the source. scope is copied from the task: joint_original when the whole unit, every owned body, the claim and its context are in this input together; segmented_original when this input holds one segment, and then reconciliation_id is copied from staged_review.segments; unresolved otherwise, with status unresolved.

A finding records what a decision must see: {id, text, adverse, classification, claim_ids, grounds}. adverse is true when the finding can lower a decision: an error, a missing hypothesis, an overstated scope, a citation used for what it does not say, a computation whose stated inputs do not cover the claim. classification is {decisions, reason}, the decisions the finding bears on and why; an adverse finding without a classification blocks every decision it might affect.

new_dependencies lists {claim_id, depends_on}, each dependency between claims that you discovered and the frame does not state; the harness widens the claim's context from it.
STAGED_RESULT_ROLE_PROMPT: Role of this series: result review. The assessed decisions are value.status, the five assurances (problem_statement, problem_openness, problem_value, problem_citations, stop) and the rubric items (A1 to A7, B1, B2, priority, attempt, accessibility, calibration), with the meanings the role text gives; staged_review.decisions names each by its path, /value/status, /value/assurances/<kind>/status or /value/rubric/<item>. objective_adequacy and method_adequacy are fixed at not_assessed and are not assessed decisions. A claim bears on a decision when the value of that decision depends on it. Every prior material objection of the record is a finding of this epoch under its objection id: it reaches the tasks that assess its claims and receives an answer before the final result.
STAGED_ADJUDICATION_ROLE_PROMPT: Role of this series: focused adjudication. The frame is the exact objection version under decision, or the documented correction, with the two completed result reviews it concerns. Two classes of units reach this series, and each unit of staged_review.units states its class: original_context (the original assessments, the original evidence and the supplied source mappings of the original pair) and current (the current problem evidence). The assessed decisions are disposition (path /disposition) and correction_admissible (path /correction_admissible). Keep the classes apart: every cell judges one unit, so a claim can have a conclusion from each class; a reason that rests on a unit names its class; a disposition may compare the conclusions of the two classes; correction_admissible true rests only on original_context grounds that demonstrate the error. Current evidence can resolve the objection. disposition is upheld, not_upheld, not_binding or unresolved. not_binding is for a material objection whose claim holds on the delivered evidence and whose contested premise does not bind the problem: cite the problem evidence that shows that the statement, its resolution criteria and its value paragraphs do not rest on that premise, or that states their dependence on it explicitly. A rubric objection is never not_binding; for it, decide only the named shortfall against bar_calibrations and rubric_definition, average no grades and waive nothing. This series is not a third vote on the problem: its claims are the objection's claim, its reason, its resolution condition and the correction request, and no task judges outside them.
FRAME_TASK_PROMPT: This is a frame task. staged_review.frame.fields lists the original fields of the frame assigned to this task, each with its source_id, its path in the record and its exact text; when the frame is split, staged_review.frame.other_tasks names the tasks that hold the other fields. staged_review.inherited lists the findings that reach this epoch from earlier reviews. Decompose the fields into claims, conditions and definitions; judge none of them. Return claims, conditions, dependencies and unresolved. claims lists the entries of kind claim and conditions the entries of kind condition or definition, each {id, kind, spans, dependencies, children}: spans lists quotations from the assigned fields, one per span the entry covers; dependencies lists the ids of the entries this one needs to be true or to be understood; children lists the ids of the parts of a compound claim, each an entry of its own, and the compound claim stays an obligation until its parts are reconciled. Extract every assessable assertion, condition and definition in the assigned fields; one field often needs several entries. Every character of every assigned field lies in the span of at least one entry: a field, or a part of a field, with no assessable content (an identifier, a date, a count) becomes an entry of kind record whose spans cover it, so that the inventory stays complete. Mentioning a field once does not account for the assertions you left out of it. dependencies lists {claim_id, depends_on} for each dependency between an entry and an entry of another task or an inherited finding. unresolved lists {text, source_ids, claim_ids}, the decomposition problems you found: a claim that cannot be stated without an unstated definition, a dependency on a field the frame does not hold, two fields that contradict each other, an inherited finding that no field addresses; it is empty only when you found none, and the harness keeps each entry as an obligation of later tasks.
READ_TASK_PROMPT: This is a read task. staged_review.units delivers the units of this task, each as its item and every artifact body it owns, with the source_id and the quotable text of each. When staged_review.task.scope is original_segment, this input holds one segment of a unit; staged_review.segments names this segment, the other segments and the reconciliation_id, and a body delivered in another segment stands as an entry with content "" and encoding "omitted". A body that several delivered units own arrives once, under the first of them, and the entry of each other unit names that unit. Read every delivered original completely. Return cards, one per delivered unit or segment, in the shape of the shared records, with findings for the findings the cards name and new_dependencies when you discover a dependency. kind is full when staged_review.task.scope is joint_original and staged_review.task.claim_ids holds every claim of the epoch; otherwise kind is fragment, and a reconciliation task writes the full card. judgments holds one cell per claim of staged_review.task.claim_ids; a card that lacks one is invalid, and so is a cell without a reason or a no_bearing cell without source_subject. The scope of each cell copies staged_review.task.scope as joint_original or segmented_original. critical_spans holds the quotations that decide the assigned claims, as many as the claims need; quote the decisive statement itself, not the sentence around it. Write establishes, conditions, conclusions and the reasons of the cells so that a reader who sees only the compact card can use them: the compact card keeps establishes, the conclusions, the conditions, the cells with their reasons, the quotations and the unresolved entries, and omits the rest of the card. For a segment, judge only what the segment shows, and put each question another segment must settle into unresolved with needs naming that segment.
CLAIM_RANGE_READ_ADDITION: staged_review.task.claim_ids is a part of the claims of the epoch; other tasks judge this unit against the other claims. Each cell here is complete on its own, and it has scope joint_original only when the whole unit, every owned body, this claim and its context are in this input together, which staged_review.task.scope states. The card of this task is a fragment; the reconciliation task of the unit unites the fragments into the full card. Name in unresolved any question that needs a claim this task does not hold.
CARD_RECONCILIATION_PROMPT: This is the reconciliation task of one unit that was read in segments or in claim ranges. staged_review.fragments delivers the fragment cards of that unit, each with the segment it covers, its cells, its findings and its verified quotations; staged_review.segments lists the segment tasks and the reconciliation_id; staged_review.units holds the original only when the task delivers it again. Return three things. First, original_checks with one record {id, task_id, group_ids, scope, status, conclusions, qualifications, conflicts, unresolved, segment_ids, reconciliation}: id is the reconciliation_id copied from staged_review.segments, task_id the id of this task, group_ids copied from staged_review.task, scope segmented_original, segment_ids the segment tasks copied from staged_review.segments, reconciliation a text that states how the segments fit together and which fragment decides each disagreement, conclusions the conclusions that hold across the segments as {id, text, grounds} with grounds quoted from the fragments' verified quotations, qualifications and conflicts the places where the fragments restrict or contradict each other, unresolved what no fragment settles; status is resolved only when conflicts and unresolved are empty. Second, cards with the full card of the unit: kind full, fragment_ids listing every fragment card, reconciliation_id copied, and judgments holding one cell per claim of the epoch with scope segmented_original and reconciliation_id, each cell weighing every fragment's judgment of that claim and naming in its reason the fragment quotations that decide it; a cell that no fragment settles is unresolved with the reason. The full card's critical_spans repeat the fragments' quotations that decide the claims; without the original you add none. Third, findings and answers where the union of the fragments shows something that no fragment shows alone. This task processes only the assigned fragments; the harness marks the card complete when every fragment is accounted for.
COMBINE_TASK_PROMPT:
This is a combination task. staged_review.combine.cards delivers compact cards: all cards of the epoch when they fit one input together, or the cards of two blocks when they do not; staged_review.combine.presentation says which (all_cards or block_pair), and staged_review.combine.blocks lists the blocks with their card ids. A compact card is the harness's projection of a full card: id, occurrence_id, establishes, evidence_type, conclusions, conditions, the cells with their status, reason and scope, the verified quotations, the finding ids, unresolved and dependencies. The full card and the original are not in this input. staged_review.claims lists the claims and conditions to consider. Find what the cards establish together that no card establishes alone: a contradiction between sources, a result that holds only under a condition another card states, a chain of dependence, a citation that one card shows and another card's source does not support, corroboration that changes what a claim rests on, a gap that no card covers.

Return combinations with one record {id, task_id, card_ids, scope, synthesis, selected_groups, segment_task_ids, reconciliation}: task_id the id of this task, card_ids every card of this input, scope joint_card, segment_task_ids empty, reconciliation null. synthesis is one text with one paragraph per claim of staged_review.claims, opened by the claim id, that states what the cards together establish about the claim and under which conditions, names the cards and quotations it rests on, and says whether an original must be read again for it. Return selected_groups, one record per combination whose originals must be read together, {id, occurrence_ids, claim_ids, question, requested_by}: occurrence_ids the units of its cards, claim_ids the claims it concerns, question what the joint reading must settle, requested_by the id of this task; the combination record's selected_groups lists their ids. Every selected group becomes an original check, so list a group because its originals must be read together, not to show coverage. No answer per pair of cards is asked for. selected_groups may be empty when no joint reading of originals is needed; then the synthesis says for each claim which interactions the quotations already settle and why none needs an original check, or that none was found and why. A question that needs a unit outside this input goes into unresolved, a list of {text, claim_ids, occurrence_ids}, with the unit named from staged_review.index. Return findings for what the cards show together.
COMBINE_SEGMENTED_PROMPT: Two cards that do not fit one input together are assessed in segments. When staged_review.task.scope is card_segment, staged_review.combine.cards delivers one segment of one compact card, with its start and end, and staged_review.combine.other_cards names the cards of the pair. Return segment_readings with one record {id, card_id, start, end, reading}: reading states, per claim of staged_review.claims, what this segment of the card shows, with the quotations it holds, and what it cannot show without the rest of the card. Make no statement about the whole of a card you saw in part. When staged_review.task.scope is segmented_card, staged_review.combine.readings delivers the segment readings of both cards and staged_review.task.segment_task_ids names their tasks. Return combinations with one record whose scope is segmented_card, card_ids both cards, segment_task_ids copied from the task, reconciliation a text that states how the segments of each card fit together, and synthesis and selected_groups under the rules of a combination task.
ORIGINAL_CHECK_TASK_PROMPT: This is an original check. staged_review.units delivers again the originals of the selected groups of this task, each unit as its item and every owned body, even where an earlier task read it; staged_review.original_check.groups lists the groups, each {id, occurrence_ids, claim_ids, question, requested_by}, and staged_review.original_check.cards their compact cards. Read the originals completely: the cards were summaries, and this task exists because a summary cannot settle the question. Return original_checks with one record {id, task_id, group_ids, scope, status, conclusions, qualifications, conflicts, unresolved, segment_ids, reconciliation}: task_id the id of this task, group_ids the ids of the groups, scope joint_original, segment_ids empty, reconciliation null. conclusions lists {id, text, grounds}, one or more per group question: text settles the question or states exactly what remains open, and grounds are quotations from the delivered originals; a conclusion without a quotation is invalid, and a conclusion that something is absent quotes the examined passage and says what it lacks. qualifications lists {occurrence_id, text, grounds}, each place where an original restricts, corrects or extends what its card said, for the questions of this task. conflicts lists {occurrence_ids, text, grounds, resolution}, each disagreement between the originals that bears on a question, with resolution naming the source that is right and why, or open with the reason. unresolved lists {text, claim_ids, needs} for what this input cannot settle. status is resolved only when conflicts and unresolved are empty, and unresolved otherwise. Return findings for what the originals show, and answers for the findings that the questions name.
ORIGINAL_CHECK_SEGMENT_ADDITION: When staged_review.task.scope is original_segment, this input holds one segment of the originals of the group, and staged_review.segments names this segment, the other segments and the reconciliation_id. Return the original check record with id equal to the id of this task, scope unresolved and status unresolved, and put what this segment shows into qualifications, conflicts and unresolved, each with quotations from this segment; the reconciliation task joins the segments. When staged_review.task.scope is segmented_original and staged_review.task.group_ids names groups, this is that reconciliation task: staged_review.segments delivers the segment records with their verified quotations. Return the original check record with id equal to the reconciliation_id, scope segmented_original, segment_ids the segment tasks, reconciliation a text that states how the segments fit together, and conclusions grounded in the segments' quotations; status is resolved only when nothing remains open.
INTEGRATE_TASK_PROMPT:
This is an integration task. staged_review.integrate delivers: conclusions, the conclusions, conditions and cells of the full cards assigned to this task, each with its id; receipts, the accepted records of the child tasks (combination records, original checks and child integrations), each with its id and its obligation ids; findings, every finding that reaches this task, inherited findings and material objections included; constraints, the decisions of this role with the claims each requires and the values the record permits so far; and copy, the identity fields of the receipt prepared for copying. A receipt records accepted work of a child task. Reconcile the inputs into one account per obligation and per claim, and state what work remains.

Return integrations with one record {id, epoch_id, task_id, selected_observations, input_roots, context_roots, child_ids, child_union, obligation_ids, dispositions, findings, answers, selected_groups, retrievals, dependencies, unresolved, decision_constraints}. Copy epoch_id, task_id, selected_observations, input_roots, context_roots, child_ids, child_union and obligation_ids from staged_review.integrate.copy; obligation_ids is the union of the assigned conclusions and the obligations of the child receipts. dispositions has exactly one entry per id of obligation_ids, {id, disposition, reason, grounds, original_check_ids}: disposition is retained (it stands), revised (an original check changed it, and original_check_ids names the resolved checks), conflict (two records disagree and no check settles it) or irrelevant-to-this-claim (it does not bear on the claim it was recorded under, and reason says what it bears on instead); grounds names the records or quotations the disposition rests on. A compact card alone, or your reading of a summary, never grounds a revision. An obligation without a disposition, a disposition without grounds, and a revised disposition without a resolved original check are invalid. For every child receipt, the dispositions of its obligations state what you keep from it; a receipt whose obligations you do not account for is invalid. dependencies lists the ids of the records this integration still needs, each a retrieval, an original check or a child integration. unresolved lists {claim_id, text, needs}, the questions that remain open, with needs naming the work that settles them. selected_groups lists the ids of the groups you select here and return in selected_groups as in a combination task, including combinations across blocks that no combination task saw together. retrievals lists the ids of the retrievals you request here under the retrieval rules below. findings lists the ids of the findings this integration carries, and answers the ids of the answers you return. An answer is {id, finding_id, disposition, reason, grounds} with disposition retained (it stays in force), answered (reason says how the named grounds address it) or unresolved; an answered disposition without grounds is invalid, and an inherited adverse finding is never dropped. decision_constraints is {permissible_assurances, permissible_decisions, decision_dependencies}: for each decision, the values the integrated record permits and the claims whose cells must be settled first; a decision whose required cells are unresolved permits no favorable value. A condition of a full card that a compact card omitted still binds; name it under the decision it binds. No decision is chosen in this task.
RETRIEVAL_RULES_PROMPT: Retrieval rules of this epoch. An integration or final task may ask for any original of the epoch again, whole or in part, by returning retrievals: [{id, question, inputs, claim_ids, context_roots, status, answer, observation_ids, requested_by}]. question states in one or two sentences what the delivery must settle. inputs lists the spans to deliver, copied from the span objects of staged_review.index or of a delivered unit; a span outside the epoch is refused. claim_ids lists the claims the question concerns and context_roots their roots, copied from staged_review.claims. status is pending, answer null, observation_ids empty, requested_by the id of this task. A request stays pending until a later task receives the spans again; that task returns the record with status resolved, answer stating what the rereading settled, and observation_ids naming the observation that delivered it. staged_review.retrieval lists the requests of this epoch so far with their status and the rereads left. A request for a question that an earlier delivery of the same spans did not settle counts against the bound of rereads; at the bound the question is recorded as unresolved, a further request for it is refused with status question_exhausted, and the task settles the question from what it has, asks a different question with a wider scope, or reports the assessment incomplete. Request what settles a named question; a request without a question, or for an original that no question needs, is not progress.
ANSWER_PAGE_TASK_PROMPT:
This is an answer task. The final result of this epoch does not fit one call, so its text fields are written in pages and its scalar choices in one terminal task. staged_review.answer identifies this page: the page fields to copy (protocol, epoch_id, role, task_id, page_id, revision, source_root, dependency_root, replaces) and ownership, the fields and list members this page owns, each {page_id, path, type, member_key, ordinal, range}. It also supplies the integrated conclusions, the assigned findings and objections with their evidence, and the references you may cite. Write only the owned fields.

Return pages with one page {protocol, epoch_id, role, task_id, page_id, revision, source_root, dependency_root, ownership, fragments, grounding, findings, dispositions, replaces}, the copied fields and ownership exactly as given. fragments has exactly one entry per ownership entry, {page_id, path, type, member_key, ordinal, range, content, grounds}, with the six ownership fields copied from that entry. type string carries a string or a segment of one: content has exactly range[1] minus range[0] characters, and the segments of one string join in order with nothing added. type object carries one list member as an object; under /value/objection_findings and /objections its id equals member_key. type empty_list carries an owned list without members, with content []. grounds lists entries copied from grounding, and grounding lists the conclusions, cells, original checks and quotations the page rests on, each as an object; every fragment ground appears in grounding. A reason field states the finding and the evidence in the words of the result review and names the conditions that bind it. An evidence field holds cite objects and source links copied from this packet under the evidence rules of the role text; a reference that no task of this epoch delivered is refused. A fragment must not set /value/status, /value/objective_adequacy, /value/method_adequacy, an assurance status or a rubric grade scalar: those belong to the terminal task. The status of a prior objection finding under /value/objection_findings (resolved, continuing or contested) and the disposition of a reassessment finding are page content and belong here. findings lists the ids of the findings this page addresses, from staged_review.answer.findings, and dispositions has exactly one entry per listed finding, {finding_id, status, reason, grounds}, with status retained, answered, unresolved, revised or conflict. An owned field without a fragment, a fragment for a field this page does not own, and an owned objection without its finding are invalid.
TERMINAL_TASK_PROMPT:
This is the terminal task. Every page of this epoch is written and verified, and the harness binds them under one composition root, a digest of the page set and its integration. staged_review.final delivers composition_root and integration_id; the integrated claims with their status; decisions, one entry per assessed decision with its path, its required claims and their cells, its supporting conclusions, its unresolved items and the values the record permits; conditions, the ids of the full-card conditions that must stay visible; and the findings with their answers. The text of the pages is in the record under the root and is not repeated. Choose only what the completed record supports.

Return terminal, assurance_checks and decision_checks. terminal is {assurances, visible_conditions, composition_root, integration_id, decisions}: assurances maps each of the five assurance kinds to passed, failed or not_assessed; visible_conditions copies the condition ids of staged_review.final.conditions; composition_root and integration_id are copied; decisions maps every scalar path that staged_review.final.decisions lists (/stage, /support, /value/status, both adequacies, the assurance statuses and the rubric scalars) to its value, with /stage result, /support null and both adequacies not_assessed. assurance_checks has one record per assurance, {id, assurance, status, claim_ids, reason, grounds, conditions_satisfied, dependencies}: claim_ids holds every claim the decision requires, grounds names the cells and conclusions the status rests on, conditions_satisfied is true only when every binding condition is met, and dependencies lists what remains open, empty for passed. decision_checks has one record per other assessed decision, {id, decision, value, claim_ids, reason, grounds, dependencies}, with decision the path. A value outside the permitted values of its decision is invalid. Use failed, and a grade below a threshold, only for an assessed defect that the grounds show. Give a grade only when the completed assessment supports it under its definition. Unfinished reviewer work supports no negative value. When the assigned work is complete and the record lacks the evidence an assurance needs, use not_assessed and name the absence in the reason; a missing part of the record justifies failed only where the criterion of the role text makes its absence a defect. When required work of this epoch is unfinished, request the material that finishes it under the retrieval rules, or return the incomplete outcome under its rules, instead of terminal. The status definitions of the role text apply, and an absent stop condition is not an assessment.
STAGED_ORDINARY_FINAL_PROMPT: Staged final of this epoch. The units of this review were read in the earlier tasks of this series, and the material for the final review fits this input, so this task writes the result review in the schema the role text defines, with the staged records beside it. The packet delivers the frame with every material objection and its evidence, and staged_review.final delivers the integrated claims with their status; the decisions with their required claims, cells, supporting conclusions, unresolved items and permitted values; the condition ids that must stay visible; the full cards with their verified quotations; every finding with its answers so far; and the cite objects and source links you may cite. An empty evidence list in this packet is not a part the record lacks: the units reached the tasks of this epoch, and their cards are here. Return one object with the fields of the result review (stage, support, value, objections, limitations, and reassessment when the context repair rules apply) and beside them terminal, assurance_checks, decision_checks, answers, findings and new_dependencies as the terminal task defines them, with composition_root null. Every assurance reason, rubric explanation and objection finding names in its text the conclusions and quotations it rests on and the conditions that bind them, and cites records by the cite objects this packet delivers; a reference that no task of this epoch delivered is refused. Every finding of staged_review.final has an answer. The rules of the terminal task for failed, not_assessed, grades and unfinished work apply. Where a decisive question remains that a rereading settles, return retrievals under the retrieval rules instead of the review; where required work of this epoch is unfinished and no retrieval finishes it, return the incomplete outcome under its rules instead.
ASSESSMENT_INCOMPLETE_PROMPT:
Incomplete outcome. A final task returns this outcome instead of a result when a required assessment of this role cannot be completed from the evidence that reached this epoch and no retrieval under the retrieval rules can complete it: a claim cell that every task left unresolved at the smallest scope, a question whose rereads reached the bound, a combination that no input holds together and whose segments do not settle it, a source that the epoch names but could not deliver. It is not a negative review: it states no status, no grade and no disposition, and the slot of this review stays occupied until the named work is done. A part that the record itself lacks, with all assigned work done, is not this case; it is assessed in the result under the rules of the terminal task.

Return assessment_incomplete as {unresolved_scope, recovery_work}, with answers for the findings you carry. unresolved_scope has one entry per unfinished item, {id, scope, cause, affected_decisions, exhausted_tasks, scope_kind, next_action}: scope is an object naming the claim ids, occurrence ids, group ids or decision the item concerns; cause states why it is unfinished; affected_decisions lists the decisions it blocks; exhausted_tasks lists the ids of the tasks that tried it; scope_kind is the scope of the last attempt (joint_original, segmented_original, joint_card, segmented_card or unresolved); next_action is {workflow, scope, prerequisite}, the research or recovery work that would finish it, where workflow names the existing command (review-assignment for new evidence or a smaller task, review-run for a task that is ready) and never a task listed in exhausted_tasks. recovery_work lists {workflow, command, payload, text}, the concrete actions and what they need first. The harness binds the known conclusions and the inherited findings from the accepted records of this epoch; do not repeat them. An entry without a cause or without a next action is invalid, and an outcome with an empty unresolved_scope is invalid: with nothing unfinished, write the result. When the unresolved scope does not fit this call, staged_review.task names answer pages for it, which you write under the answer task rules with the paths /known_conclusions, /unresolved_scope, /findings and /recovery_work.
CONTEXT_REPAIR_STAGED_PROMPT: Context repair rules of this epoch. This epoch reassesses after recorded context contamination; it is not a new blind review. The historical inputs, the observed assessments and the unresolved objections remain evidence, and their former independence is not currently qualified. The result carries one more top-level member, reassessment: {assignment_id, findings: [{review_id, disposition, reason, evidence}]}, with assignment_id copied from context_repair and one finding for every inherited final review of this phase. Label a review confirmed only when the effective result repeats its support, value, objections and limitations exactly; when anything changes, including wording, label it revised; label it unresolved when the record cannot settle it; give the supplied evidence for a revised or unresolved finding. A changed judgment alone does not dispose of a historical material objection: it receives its finding in objection_findings like every prior objection, and objections lists only the objections you raise yourself. In a paged final, the reassessment is the owned field /reassessment of its answer page.
STAGED_ADJUDICATION_ANSWER_ADDITION: In a focused adjudication a page owns /reason, /evidence, or a segment of one of them, and nothing else. reason states the finding on the objection version from the integrated record and keeps the original_context grounds apart from the current grounds, naming the class of each. evidence holds references copied from this packet under the evidence rules of the adjudicator, and names no current evidence as a ground of correction admissibility. /objection_id, /disposition and /correction_admissible are terminal choices, and a fragment that sets one is invalid.
STAGED_ADJUDICATION_TERMINAL_PROMPT: This is the terminal task of a focused adjudication. staged_review.final delivers composition_root and integration_id; the integrated claims with their status and the class of each conclusion; decisions, the entries for disposition and correction_admissible with their required claims, cells, supporting conclusions, unresolved items and permitted values; and the condition ids that must stay visible. Return terminal, decision_checks and answers. terminal is {objection_id, disposition, correction_admissible, visible_conditions, composition_root, integration_id, decisions}: objection_id copied from the frame, visible_conditions copied from staged_review.final.conditions, decisions mapping /objection_id, /disposition and /correction_admissible to their values. decision_checks has one record per decision, {id, decision, value, claim_ids, reason, grounds, dependencies}: for disposition, claim_ids holds every claim of the epoch, grounds names the settled cells and conclusions, reason names the class of each ground, and dependencies is empty; for correction_admissible, grounds names original_context records only. The rules of the role series text for disposition and not_binding apply. An unsettled required cell supports unresolved only, and correction_admissible is null when no correction is requested. When a rereading within the frozen dispute can still settle a remaining question, return retrievals under the retrieval rules instead. When required work of this epoch is unfinished and no retrieval finishes it, return the incomplete outcome under its rules; it is not a disposition, and the objection stays open.
STAGED_ADJUDICATION_FINAL_PROMPT: Staged final of this adjudication. The material fits this input, so this task returns the adjudicator object the role text defines (objection_id, disposition, reason, evidence, correction_admissible) and beside it terminal, decision_checks and answers as the terminal task of a focused adjudication defines them, with composition_root null. staged_review.final delivers the integrated claims with their status and the class of each conclusion, the two decisions with their required claims, cells, supporting conclusions and permitted values, the full cards with their verified quotations, and the references you may cite. reason names the conclusions and quotations it rests on and keeps original_context grounds apart from current grounds. Where a rereading within the frozen dispute can still settle a decisive question, return retrievals under the retrieval rules instead of the object; where required work of this epoch is unfinished and no retrieval finishes it, return the incomplete outcome under its rules instead.
SEGMENT_OMITTED_BODY_NOTE: This artifact body is not part of the segment that this task reads. Another segment listed in staged_review.segments carries it, in its own task. Judge only what this segment shows, and name in unresolved any question that needs this body.
SHARED_BODY_NOTE: This artifact body is delivered once in this task, under the unit that this entry names by key and index. This unit owns the same body. Read it there, and judge the claims of this unit on it as well.
REREAD_DELIVERY_NOTE: This original is delivered again for the retrieval whose id this delivery names. Its bytes are the same as its first delivery in this epoch. Settle the question of that retrieval from it and return the retrieval record with status resolved.
QUESTION_EXHAUSTED_NOTE: This request repeats a question that the earlier deliveries of this epoch did not settle, and the bound of rereads for an unchanged question is reached. The original is not delivered again, and the question is recorded as unresolved. Settle it from the record, ask a different question with a wider scope, or report the assessment incomplete.
QUOTATION_UNMATCHED_NOTE: The harness did not find this text in the source that source_id names, so the record that carried it received no credit. Quote the source character for character, or ground the record in another way.
